title: Tony's Pizza buys a package: the CPP and the CGL
summary: Build Tony's package policy, watch CGL Coverages A, B and C at work in one Detroit week, then follow a caterer through claims-made tails.
objectives: Name the building blocks of a commercial package policy
Match CGL Coverages A, B and C to what they pay and how they trigger
Place a claim in the general or the products-completed operations aggregate
Apply the claims-made retroactive date and the basic and supplemental tails

scenes.title: Tony's Pizza buys a package: the CPP and the CGL
scenes.subtitle: How a package is built, what CGL Coverages A, B and C pay, and how claims-made tails work (2013 ISO CGL)

draw.text: One policy for all of it?

beats.text: Tony's Pizza in Detroit faces a rough week: a torn mat, a slogan fight, a wet floor.
beats.say: Tony's Pizza in Detroit faces a rough week: a torn mat, a slogan fight, a wet floor.

beats.text: Commercial package questions are 12% of your exam, about 18 items. Let's build Tony's policy.
beats.say: Commercial package questions are twelve percent of your exam, about eighteen items. Let's build Tony's policy.

scenes.title: What's inside Tony's package?
scenes.src: IRMI glossary; ISO IL DS 00 09 08; IL 00 17 11 98, A-F; IL 04 15 04 98; CP 00 10 10 12; questions comm-001, comm-002

draw.text: Insurer's notice to cancel: 10 days for nonpayment, 30 for other reasons
Audit: up to 3 years after the policy
Vacancy? Not one of the six: a property loss condition

spots.label: Common Policy Declarations
spots.text: Page one: the named insured, the policy period, the coverage parts that make up the policy, and a premium for each part plus the total.

spots.label: Common Policy Conditions
spots.text: Six conditions for every coverage part: cancellation, changes, examination of books, inspections, premiums, and transfer of rights.

spots.label: Interline endorsement
spots.text: Modifies more than one coverage part. Protective Safeguards, for one, modifies both the commercial property and farm parts.

spots.label: Coverage part: commercial property
spots.text: Covers Tony's own property: his building, plus his business personal property, the business things in it or within 100 feet.

spots.label: Coverage part: general liability
spots.text: Tony's liability coverage. Coverage A, for one, pays injury and damage he legally owes others, plus defense. Two parts in one policy: a package.

beats.text: Dana, I want one policy for my building and my customers.
beats.say: Dana, I want one policy for my building and my customers.

beats.text: One way is a commercial package policy: property and liability coverage for a business, in one policy. Tap each part.
beats.say: One way is a commercial package policy: property and liability coverage for a business, in one policy. Tap each part.

reveal.text: A package is common declarations and conditions, plus coverage parts. One part alone is monoline; two or more make a package.
reveal.say: A package is common declarations and conditions, plus coverage parts. One part alone is monoline; two or more make a package.

reveal.text: Under the 1998 conditions, the insurer gives 10 days' notice to cancel for nonpayment, 30 for other reasons. State amendatory endorsements can change that.
reveal.say: Under the nineteen ninety-eight conditions, the insurer gives ten days' notice to cancel for nonpayment, thirty for other reasons. State amendatory endorsements can change that.

reveal.text: It may audit the books up to 3 years after the policy. Watch out: vacancy isn't one of the six. It's a property loss condition.
reveal.say: It may audit the books up to three years after the policy. Watch out: vacancy isn't one of the six. It's a property loss condition.

scenes.title: Tony's CGL: Coverages A and B
scenes.src: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. I Cov. A 1.a-b, Cov. B 1.a-b; Sec. V defs. 13, 14

draw.text:
My ankle!
See you in court.
A: bodily injury and property damage, plus defense

beats.text: Now Tony's CGL, short for commercial general liability, 2013 edition. Monday, a customer trips on a torn mat, breaks her ankle and sues.
beats.say: Now Tony's C G L, short for commercial general liability, twenty thirteen edition. Monday, a customer trips on a torn mat, breaks her ankle and sues.

beats.text: Coverage A pays bodily injury and property damage Tony legally owes, plus defense. The trigger: an occurrence, an accident, causing injury during the policy period.
beats.say: Coverage A pays bodily injury and property damage Tony legally owes, plus defense. The trigger: an occurrence, an accident, causing injury during the policy period.

beats.text: Tuesday, a rival sues, saying Tony's ad uses her slogan. Coverage B pays personal and advertising injury, for an offense committed during the policy period.
beats.say: Tuesday, a rival sues, saying Tony's ad uses her slogan. Coverage B pays personal and advertising injury, for an offense committed during the policy period.

scenes.title: Coverage B: the four Ps
scenes.src: Hook mn-mn_comm-03; ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. V def. 14; question comm-009
scenes.hook: Coverage B's four Ps: Police, Property, Publication, Promotion.
items: Police: false arrest, detention or imprisonment; malicious prosecution
Property: wrongful eviction, wrongful entry, invasion of private occupancy
Publication: slander, libel, disparagement; violating a right of privacy
Promotion: using another's ad idea; copyright, trade dress or slogan in your ad

draw.text: Hurt by a defective product? Coverage A, not B

beats.text: Coverage B's offenses come in four Ps: Police, Property, Publication, Promotion.
beats.say: Coverage B's offenses come in four P's: Police, Property, Publication, Promotion.

beats.text: Police: false arrest, detention or imprisonment, and malicious prosecution. Property: wrongful eviction, wrongful entry, or invasion of private occupancy.
beats.say: Police: false arrest, detention or imprisonment, and malicious prosecution. Property: wrongful eviction, wrongful entry, or invasion of private occupancy.

beats.text: Publication: slander, libel, disparagement, or violating a right of privacy. Promotion: using another's ad idea, or infringing on a copyright, trade dress or slogan in your ad, like Tony's ad using her slogan.
beats.say: Publication: slander, libel, disparagement, or violating a right of privacy. Promotion: using another's ad idea, or infringing on a copyright, trade dress or slogan in your ad, like Tony's ad using her slogan.

beats.text: Watch out: injury from a defective product is Coverage A, not B.
beats.say: Watch out: injury from a defective product is Coverage A, not B.

scenes.title: Tony's call: the slip on the wet floor
scenes.src: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. I Cov. C 1.a-b; question comm-007

draw.text:
I'm not suing.
I just have this bill.

beats.text: Wednesday, a regular slips on Tony's wet floor and sprains his wrist.
beats.say: Wednesday, a regular slips on Tony's wet floor and sprains his wrist.

beats.text: I'm not suing, Tony. I just have this bill.
beats.say: I'm not suing, Tony. I just have this bill.
beats.speaker: Customer

beats.text: Coverage C pays medical expenses for accidents on Tony's premises or from his operations, regardless of fault. Under the 2013 CGL, they must be incurred and reported within 1 year. What does Tony do?
beats.say: Coverage C pays medical expenses for accidents on Tony's premises or from his operations, regardless of fault. Under the twenty thirteen C G L, they must be incurred and reported within one year. What does Tony do?

options.label: Not my fault. Tell him tough luck.
options.fail: Coverage C pays medical expenses for accidents on Tony's premises regardless of fault. Nobody has to prove he was careless.

beats.text: Tony waves him off and hides behind the oven. But Coverage C pays regardless of fault.
beats.say: Tony waves him off and hides behind the oven. But Coverage C pays regardless of fault.

options.label: Sit on the bills for 14 months
options.fail: Coverage C pays only expenses incurred and reported within 1 year of the accident. Fourteen months is too late.

beats.text: Fourteen months later, Tony mails the bills. Too late: they must be incurred and reported within 1 year.
beats.say: Fourteen months later, Tony mails the bills. Too late: they must be incurred and reported within one year.

options.label: Report it now, under Coverage C
options.win: Coverage C pays medical expenses for accidents on Tony's premises, regardless of fault, if incurred and reported within 1 year.

beats.text: Tony reports it now. Coverage C pays his bill, no fault needed.
beats.say: Tony reports it now. Coverage C pays his bill, no fault needed.

reveal.text: No fault needed, but a 1-year clock.
reveal.say: No fault needed, but a one-year clock.

scenes.title: Coverage A, B or C?
scenes.src: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. I Cov. A 1.a, Cov. B 1.a, Cov. C 1.a-b; Sec. V def. 14; hook mn-mn_comm-02; question comm-009

cards.text: A family takes Tony's pizza home. A bad topping makes them sick, and they sue.
cards.why: Bodily injury from Tony's product is Coverage A. It's not a Coverage B offense.

cards.text: Tony wrongly accuses a customer of stealing and holds him until police come. He sues for false arrest.
cards.why: False arrest and detention is a Police offense: Coverage B.

cards.text: A boy bumps his head on Tony's counter. His mom just wants the doctor bill paid. Nobody blames Tony.
cards.why: Medical expenses from an accident on Tony's premises, paid regardless of fault: Coverage C.

cards.text: A rival sues Tony for libel over a flyer he handed out about her pizza.
cards.why: Libel is a Publication offense: Coverage B.

cards.text: A shelf at Tony's falls and smashes a customer's laptop. She sues for the damage.
cards.why: Property damage that Tony legally owes for is Coverage A.

beats.text: Your turn: Coverage A, B or C?
beats.say: Your turn: Coverage A, B or C?

reveal.text: A is for Accidents, B for Big mouth, C for Care. Even injury from Tony's product is A.
reveal.say: A is for Accidents, B for Big mouth, C for Care. Even injury from Tony's product is A.

scenes.title: Supplementary payments ride on top
scenes.src: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Supplementary Payments - Coverages A and B, 1.a-g; hook mn-mn_comm-04; questions comm-005, comm-006

draw.text: Court costs taxed against Tony: paid
Attorney fees taxed against Tony: not paid

beats.text: Supplementary payments for Coverages A and B don't reduce the limits. They ride on top, like a canoe on the roof rack heading Up North.
beats.say: Supplementary payments for Coverages A and B don't reduce the limits. They ride on top, like a canoe on the roof rack heading Up North.

beats.text: Under the 2013 CGL: up to $250 for bail bonds after an accident or traffic violation in a covered vehicle. And up to $250 a day for Tony's lost earnings helping the defense.
beats.say: Under the twenty thirteen C G L: up to two hundred fifty dollars for bail bonds after an accident or traffic violation in a covered vehicle. And up to two hundred fifty dollars a day for Tony's lost earnings helping the defense.

beats.text: Court costs taxed against Tony, meaning the court orders him to pay, are paid. Attorney fees taxed against him aren't. Watch that trap.
beats.say: Court costs taxed against Tony, meaning the court orders him to pay, are paid. Attorney fees taxed against him aren't. Watch that trap.

scenes.title: Two buckets of limits
scenes.src: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. III 2-5 and annual period; Sec. V def. 16.a; adapted from hook mn-mn_comm-02; question comm-008
scenes.plain: Injury or damage away from premises you own or rent, from your product or finished work. Its own aggregate covers Coverage A only.
scenes.example: Tony's pizza makes a family sick at home: products bucket. A customer trips in his shop: general aggregate.
scenes.exam: General aggregate: Coverage A except products-completed ops, plus all of B and C. Work still in progress isn't completed ops.

draw.text: rest of A, all of B and C
Each occurrence limit: A plus C

beats.text: CGL limits work like two buckets: yearly caps called aggregates. One is for the products-completed operations hazard: injury or damage away from premises you own or rent, from your product or finished work.
beats.say: C G L limits work like two buckets: yearly caps called aggregates. One is for the products-completed operations hazard: injury or damage away from premises you own or rent, from your product or finished work.

beats.text: It holds only Coverage A, like a family sick from Tony's pizza at home. A customer who trips in his shop goes in the other bucket: the general aggregate.
beats.say: It holds only Coverage A, like a family sick from Tony's pizza at home. A customer who trips in his shop goes in the other bucket: the general aggregate.

beats.text: Everything else fills the general aggregate: the rest of A, plus all of B and C. Work still in progress isn't completed operations.
beats.say: Everything else fills the general aggregate: the rest of A, plus all of B and C. Work still in progress isn't completed operations.

beats.text: The each occurrence limit caps A plus C from one occurrence.
beats.say: The each occurrence limit caps A plus C from one occurrence.

scenes.title: Which bucket does it fill?
scenes.src: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Sec. III 2-3; Sec. V def. 16.a; questions comm-008, comm-cpa-01

items.text: A server spills hot soup on a diner, who sues
items.why: Premises and operations: Coverage A, general aggregate.

items.text: A delivery customer cracks a tooth on Tony's pizza at home
items.why: Tony's product, away from his premises: products bucket.

items.text: The rival's slogan suit against Tony
items.why: All of Coverage B counts in the general aggregate.

items.text: No-fault medical bill: a diner slips inside Tony's
items.why: Coverage C: all of C counts in the general aggregate.

items.text: Mid-framing, a contractor's board hits a passerby
items.why: Work in progress isn't completed ops: general aggregate.

items.text: Contractor's finished railing at a client's hurts a guest
items.why: Finished work, away from the contractor's premises: completed operations.

beats.text: Your turn. Which bucket does each claim fill?
beats.say: Your turn. Which bucket does each claim fill?

reveal.text: Product or finished work away from your premises: products bucket.
reveal.say: Product or finished work away from your premises: products bucket.

reveal.text: Everything else, even work in progress: general aggregate.
reveal.say: Everything else, even work in progress: general aggregate.

scenes.title: Occurrence or claims-made: which date counts?
scenes.src: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Cov. A 1.b; CG 00 02 04 13 per FC&S (2014), Austin and Stanovich (2012), form text not seen

draw.text: Claim first made in the policy period

beats.text: Tony's CGL is an occurrence form: injury during the policy period triggers it, even if the claim comes years later. No retro date, and no extra reporting time needed.
beats.say: Tony's C G L is an occurrence form: injury during the policy period triggers it, even if the claim comes years later. No retro date, and no extra reporting time needed.

beats.text: Dana's client Grace is a Lansing caterer.
beats.say: Dana's client Grace is a Lansing caterer.

beats.text: Mine's claims-made. What changes?
beats.say: Mine's claims-made. What changes?
beats.speaker: Grace

beats.text: The trigger: a claim first made during the policy period, for injury after the retroactive date and before the policy ends. That can even be injury before the policy began.
beats.say: The trigger: a claim first made during the policy period, for injury after the retroactive date and before the policy ends. That can even be injury before the policy began.

beats.text: So find the trigger date: the injury, or the first claim.
beats.say: So find the trigger date: the injury, or the first claim.

scenes.q: Grace's claims-made CGL runs January 1, 2025, to January 1, 2026, with a retroactive date of January 1, 2023. A guest hurt at a 2022 event first makes a claim in May 2025. The claim is:
choices: Covered: the claim was first made during the policy period
Not covered: the injury came before the retroactive date
Not covered: claims-made only pays injury during the policy period
scenes.why: Injury before the retro date isn't covered, even when the claim is first made during the policy period. Injury after the retro date, but before the policy began, can be.

beats.text: Your turn: listen for the dates. Covered or not?
beats.say: Your turn: listen for the dates. Covered or not?

reveal.text: Not covered: the injury came before the retroactive date, even though the claim came during the policy period.
reveal.say: Not covered: the injury came before the retroactive date, even though the claim came during the policy period.

scenes.src: CG 00 02 04 13 per FC&S (2014), Austin and Stanovich (2012), form text not seen; question comm-014

scenes.title: Two tails: more time to make a claim
scenes.src: CG 00 02 04 13 as described by FC&S (2014) and Austin and Stanovich (2012); form text not seen; hook mn-mn_comm-05
scenes.plain: A tail: extra time after a claims-made policy ends to make claims, for injury after the retro date and before the policy ended.
scenes.example: Like leaving the porch light on after a party: late knocks still get answered, but only from guests who were at the party, never from new arrivals.
scenes.exam: Supplemental tail: request in writing within 60 days; costs up to 200% of the annual premium; unlimited; reinstates the aggregates.

draw.text: supplemental tail: starts after basic, no end

beats.text: A claims-made policy that's canceled, nonrenewed or replaced by occurrence coverage gets an extended reporting period: a tail. That's extra time after the policy ends to make claims, for injury after the retro date and before the policy ended.
beats.say: A claims-made policy that's canceled, nonrenewed or replaced by occurrence coverage gets an extended reporting period: a tail. That's extra time after the policy ends to make claims, for injury after the retro date and before the policy ended.

beats.text: Under the 2013 claims-made CGL, the basic tail is free and automatic. It gives 60 days for occurrences never reported, and 5 years for those reported no later than 60 days after the end.
beats.say: Under the twenty thirteen claims-made C G L, the basic tail is free and automatic. It gives sixty days for occurrences never reported, and five years for those reported no later than sixty days after the end.

beats.text: The supplemental tail is optional: request it, in writing, within 60 days after the policy ends. It starts when the basic tail ends, costs up to 200% of the annual premium, never ends, and reinstates the aggregates.
beats.say: The supplemental tail is optional: request it, in writing, within sixty days after the policy ends. It starts when the basic tail ends, costs up to two hundred percent of the annual premium, never ends, and reinstates the aggregates.

beats.text: Neither tail covers injury after the policy ends.
beats.say: Neither tail covers injury after the policy ends.

beats.text: A tail is like leaving the porch light on after a party that started at the retro date. Late knocks still get answered, but only from guests who were at the party, never from new arrivals.
beats.say: A tail is like leaving the porch light on after a party that started at the retro date. Late knocks still get answered, but only from guests who were at the party, never from new arrivals.

scenes.title: Grace's call: one last event
scenes.src: CG 00 02 04 13 per FC&S (2014) and Austin and Stanovich (2012), form text not seen; questions comm-015, comm-016

beats.text: December 2025. Grace is retiring and won't renew. Her claims-made policy, 2013 form, ends January 1. Its retro date is January 1, 2023. Tonight a guest trips at her last event. No claim yet. What should Grace do?
beats.say: December twenty twenty-five. Grace is retiring and won't renew. Her claims-made policy, twenty thirteen form, ends January first. Its retro date is January first, twenty twenty-three. Tonight a guest trips at her last event. No claim yet. What should Grace do?

options.label: Do nothing. The policy covered that night.
options.fail: Claims-made looks at the claim date. An occurrence she never reported gets just 60 days of basic tail, and this claim came months later.

beats.text: In August, the guest sues. The fall was never reported, so the free tail lasted only 60 days. No coverage.
beats.say: In August, the guest sues. The fall was never reported, so the free tail lasted only sixty days. No coverage.

draw.text: Never reported: the tail was 60 days

But I was insured
that night!

options.label: Report the guest's fall to her insurer now
options.win: Reported before the policy ends, or no later than 60 days after, an occurrence gets the free basic tail: claims can come up to 5 years after.

beats.text: Grace reports it tonight. When the guest sues in August, the basic tail covers it: reported in time, so 5 years.
beats.say: Grace reports it tonight. When the guest sues in August, the basic tail covers it: reported in time, so five years.

options.label: Buy the supplemental tail next spring
options.fail: The supplemental tail must be requested in writing within 60 days after the policy ends. April is too late, and the unreported fall got only 60 days.

beats.text: In April, Grace asks for the supplemental tail. Too late: the written request was due within 60 days.
beats.say: In April, Grace asks for the supplemental tail. Too late: the written request was due within sixty days.

draw.text: Can I still buy the tail?

reveal.text: Report before the end, or no later than 60 days after, and the free tail runs 5 years.
reveal.say: Report before the end, or no later than sixty days after, and the free tail runs five years.

scenes.title: Key takeaways
items: Package: common declarations and conditions plus 2 or more parts
A: injury and damage. B: the four Ps. C: med pay, no fault, 1 year
Supplementary payments ride on top: $250 bail bonds, $250 a day
Products-completed operations has its own aggregate
Claims-made: check the retro date; basic tail 60 days or 5 years

beats.text: A package is common declarations and conditions plus two or more parts. A is injury and damage, B the four Ps, C med pay: no fault needed, but a 1-year clock. Supplementary payments ride on top: up to $250 for bail bonds, $250 a day for lost earnings.
beats.say: A package is common declarations and conditions plus two or more parts. A is injury and damage, B the four P's, C med pay: no fault needed, but a one-year clock. Supplementary payments ride on top: up to two hundred fifty dollars for bail bonds, two hundred fifty dollars a day for lost earnings.

beats.text: Products-completed operations get their own aggregate: their own bucket. On claims-made, check the retro date. The basic tail is 60 days, or 5 years for occurrences reported no later than 60 days after the end.
beats.say: Products-completed operations get their own aggregate: their own bucket. On claims-made, check the retro date. The basic tail is sixty days, or five years for occurrences reported no later than sixty days after the end.
